name: Michael Johnson
chief_complaint: Worsening shortness of breath and ankle swelling over the past 3 days
opening_statement: I've been having trouble breathing, especially when I lie down at night. My ankles have become quite swollen, and I can't walk to the letterbox without getting puffed.
emotional_baseline: Anxious and concerned, with visible relief when seated upright. Cooperative but appears fatigued.

symptoms.onset: Gradually worsening over 3 days, previously stable on background NYHA Class II
symptoms.character: Orthopnoea requiring 3 pillows, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea waking patient at 2am
symptoms.severity: NYHA Class III-IV, cannot walk 50 metres on flat ground
symptoms.timing: Constant at rest, worse with minimal exertion
symptoms.exacerbating_factors: Lying flat, minimal exertion, cold weather
symptoms.associated_symptoms: Peripheral oedema, reduced exercise tolerance, fatigue

rag_citations.excerpt: Acute decompensated heart failure presents with dyspnoea at rest or minimal exertion, orthopnoea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, and peripheral oedema
rag_citations.context: Clinical presentation of acute heart failure exacerbation

symptoms.onset: Progressive over 5 days, pitting to mid-shin level
symptoms.character: Symmetrical, pitting, extends to knees bilaterally
symptoms.severity: 3+ pitting oedema, weight gain of 4kg in one week
symptoms.exacerbating_factors: Prolonged standing, increased salt intake at family BBQ 5 days ago

rag_citations.excerpt: Peripheral oedema in heart failure results from fluid retention due to reduced cardiac output and neurohumoral activation. Weight gain >2kg in 3 days suggests fluid overload
rag_citations.context: Pathophysiology of fluid retention in heart failure

symptoms.character: Generalised weakness, inability to complete ADLs without rest
symptoms.severity: Unable to shower without sitting, walks 20 metres before stopping

rag_citations.excerpt: Reduced exercise tolerance in heart failure reflects decreased cardiac output and skeletal muscle perfusion, manifesting as fatigue and early onset of dyspnoea
rag_citations.context: Functional limitations in chronic heart failure

symptoms.onset: Waking 3-4 times per night for past week
symptoms.timing: Nocturnal, starting 1-2 hours after lying down

rag_citations.excerpt: Nocturia in heart failure occurs due to redistribution of peripheral oedema fluid when supine, increasing renal perfusion and urine production

past_medical_history.condition: Chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
past_medical_history.details: EF 35% on echo 2024, ischaemic cardiomyopathy post-MI 2019, NYHA Class II baseline
Anterior STEMI treated with primary PCI to LAD, drug-eluting stent deployed, residual LV dysfunction
past_medical_history.current_status: Stable CAD, on optimal medical therapy

past_medical_history.details: HbA1c 7.2% (last 3 months), on metformin and empagliflozin, no microvascular complications
Previously well-controlled on ramipril, recent home readings 160/90 mmHg despite compliance
On high-intensity statin therapy, LDL 2.1 mmol/L (target <1.8 for secondary prevention)

medications.name: Frusemide
medications.compliance: Good, patient reports reduced urine output past 3 days despite compliance

allergies: No known drug allergies (NKDA). Seasonal hay fever to grass pollen (non-drug).
family_history: Father died age 68 from myocardial infarction. Mother died age 82 from stroke. One brother alive, age 72, has hypertension and Type 2 diabetes. No family history of sudden cardiac death or inherited cardiomyopathies.

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife in single-storey home, toilet upstairs, bedroom downstairs
social_history.alcohol: Nil current, previously 10-15 standard drinks/week, ceased 2019
social_history.exercise: Previously walked 30 minutes daily, now limited to 50 metres due to dyspnoea
social_history.diet: Wife cooks meals, attended family BBQ 5 days ago (high salt intake), otherwise low-salt diet
social_history.supports: Wife (primary carer), daughter lives 20km away, visits weekly, independent with ADLs when well

examination_findings.general: Alert, anxious, appears fatigued. Sitting upright in chair, using accessory muscles. No cyanosis.

cardiovascular.jvp: Elevated 8cm above sternal angle at 45 degrees
cardiovascular.heart_sounds: Dual heart sounds, soft S3 gallop present, no murmurs
cardiovascular.oedema: 3+ pitting oedema to knees bilaterally, sacral oedema present

respiratory.inspection: Tachypnoeic, using accessory muscles, no chest wall deformity
respiratory.auscultation: Bibasal fine inspiratory crackles to mid-zones, no wheeze

examination_findings.abdominal: Soft, non-tender, liver edge palpable 3cm below costal margin (hepatomegaly), positive hepatojugular reflux, no ascites detected
examination_findings.other: Capillary refill <2 seconds, no clinical jaundice, no asterixis

initial.result: Sinus rhythm 96 bpm, pathological Q waves V1-V4 (old anterior MI), no acute ST changes
initial.interpretation: Previous anterior MI, no acute ischaemia

initial.result: Cardiomegaly (CTR 0.62), bilateral perihilar alveolar infiltrates (bat-wing pattern), Kerley B lines, small bilateral pleural effusions, upper lobe diversion
initial.interpretation: Acute pulmonary oedema, moderate heart failure
Markedly elevated, consistent with acute decompensated heart failure

pathology.result: Na 134 mmol/L, K 4.8 mmol/L, Creatinine 145 μmol/L (baseline 120), eGFR 42 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD Stage 3a)
pathology.interpretation: Mild hyponatraemia, acute-on-chronic kidney injury, hyperkalaemia borderline
Mildly elevated due to chronic HFrEF, no acute MI

pathology.result: Bilirubin 28 μmol/L, ALT 45 U/L, ALP 120 U/L, GGT 85 U/L
pathology.interpretation: Mild hepatic congestion secondary to right heart failure

imaging.result: LV EF 35%, severe LV systolic dysfunction (akinetic anterior/apical walls), mild MR (functional), LVEDD 6.2cm, no pericardial effusion
imaging.interpretation: HFrEF, ischaemic cardiomyopathy, no interval change from 2023

expected_management.rationale: Hypoxia correction, eTG: Supplemental oxygen for SpO2 <90% in acute heart failure
Diuresis for volume overload, eTG: IV loop diuretics first-line for acute pulmonary oedema
Monitor for arrhythmias, electrolyte disturbances during diuresis
Target negative 1-2L daily, monitor diuretic response
Monitor for worsening renal function, electrolyte derangement (hypokalaemia, hyperkalaemia)
ACEI therapy reduces mortality in HFrEF, monitor for hypotension

expected_management.action: Continue bisoprolol 10mg daily (do not cease in acute setting)
expected_management.rationale: Beta-blocker withdrawal increases mortality, continue unless cardiogenic shock

expected_management.action: Hold metformin if creatinine >150 μmol/L or rising
expected_management.rationale: Risk of lactic acidosis in acute kidney injury

expected_management.action: Consider IV GTN infusion if SBP >110 mmHg and persisting dyspnoea
expected_management.rationale: Reduces preload/afterload, eTG: Nitrates for acute heart failure if not hypotensive

expected_management.action: Repeat CXR in 24 hours to assess diuretic response
expected_management.rationale: Objective measure of pulmonary oedema resolution

expected_management.action: Coronary angiography review (if not done recently)
expected_management.rationale: Exclude new ischaemic event as precipitant, check stent patency

expected_management.action: Cardiology review for consideration of cardiac resynchronisation therapy (CRT) or ICD
expected_management.rationale: EF <35% despite optimal medical therapy, NYHA III-IV symptoms

expected_management.action: Heart failure nurse education on salt restriction (<2g/day), daily weights, diuretic self-titration
MBS referral for Home Medicines Review (HMR)
expected_management.rationale: MBS item 900: Optimise polypharmacy, check compliance, identify precipitants

critical_errors.description: Failing to administer oxygen and IV diuretics immediately
critical_errors.consequence: Respiratory failure, cardiac arrest, preventable death from pulmonary oedema

critical_errors.description: Ceasing beta-blocker (bisoprolol) in acute heart failure without cardiogenic shock
critical_errors.consequence: Increased mortality risk, beta-blocker withdrawal syndrome, rebound tachycardia

critical_errors.description: Not monitoring renal function and electrolytes during aggressive diuresis
critical_errors.consequence: Undetected acute kidney injury, dangerous hypokalaemia/hyperkalaemia, arrhythmias

critical_errors.description: Discharging patient without heart failure education or follow-up plan
critical_errors.consequence: High readmission risk (50% within 6 months), missed device therapy opportunity

critical_errors.description: Not exploring precipitant for acute decompensation (dietary indiscretion at BBQ)
critical_errors.consequence: Missed opportunity for preventative education, recurrent admissions

critical_errors.description: Not calculating fluid restriction target or educating patient on daily weights
critical_errors.consequence: Suboptimal self-management, delayed recognition of future decompensation

fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP (Cardiology), Staff Specialist, Royal Prince Alfred Hospital
fracp_reviews.comments: Clinically accurate representation of acute decompensated heart failure in elderly patient with ischaemic cardiomyopathy. Difficulty calibration appropriate (Medium) given 4 comorbidities and time-critical management. NT-proBNP value realistic for this presentation. Management plan aligns with NHFA/CSANZ 2024 guidelines and eTG recommendations. Critical errors correctly identify life-threatening omissions (oxygen/diuretics) and common pitfall (beta-blocker cessation). Suggest candidates also consider infection screen as potential precipitant. Strong educational value for AMC clinical exam preparation.

fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP (General Medicine), Clinical Senior Lecturer, University of Sydney
fracp_reviews.comments: Well-constructed case reflecting real-world presentation seen in Australian general medicine units. Social history detail (BBQ with high salt intake) provides realistic precipitant for teaching purposes. Medication list appropriately reflects optimal guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for HFrEF including SGLT2i. Investigations section correctly includes Australian-relevant MBS items (item 900 for HMR). Learning objectives cover essential competencies: acute heart failure management, diuretic dosing, device therapy indications, and patient education. FRACP trainees would benefit from considering CRT-D vs ICD-only decision-making in this case. Approved without reservations.

learning_objectives: Recognise clinical features of acute decompensated heart failure (NYHA classification, orthopnoea, PND, peripheral oedema)
Differentiate chronic stable heart failure from acute exacerbation requiring hospital admission
Apply eTG/NHFA guidelines for immediate management: oxygen, IV diuretics, monitoring, and positioning
Understand precipitants of acute decompensation: dietary indiscretion, infection, arrhythmia, medication non-compliance, ischaemia
Recognise importance of continuing beta-blockers in acute heart failure (unless cardiogenic shock/hypotension)
Interpret NT-proBNP levels in context of age and clinical presentation (>450 pg/mL diagnostic threshold age >50)
Identify candidates for device therapy: CRT (LBBB + EF <35% + NYHA III-IV) and ICD (EF <35% + 40 days post-MI)
Apply Australian-specific resources: MBS Home Medicines Review (item 900), PBS restrictions for SGLT2 inhibitors in HFrEF
